About the Role
 Our client is seeking a Senior AWS DataHub Developer to design and build real-time, event-driven data services on AWS. This role is developer-first (application-side) rather than infrastructure-led. You will architect and deliver Kafka-based streaming pipelines and serverless data applications that ingest, transform, and serve data at scale.
 You’ll collaborate with architects, data engineers, and product teams to deliver secure, resilient, observable, and highly scalable solutions that power enterprise-grade analytics and event-driven applications.
 What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities)
 Design & Deliver Event-Driven Pipelines: Build serverless data flows using AWS Lambda, Step Functions, EventBridge, SNS, SQS, API Gateway.
 Real-Time Streaming: Develop Kafka (Apache Kafka/Amazon MSK) consumers/producers for high-throughput, low-latency streaming and decoupled microservices.
 Microservices & APIs: Build and optimize TypeScript (preferred) or Python services/APIs for data ingestion, transformation, and delivery.
 AWS Data Services Integration: Work with S3, DynamoDB, Glue, Athena, CloudWatch for storage, metadata, querying, and observability.
 Quality & Reliability: Implement idempotency, retries, dead-letter queues, exactly-once/at-least-once semantics where appropriate, and schema evolution strategies.

 Agile Collaboration: Contribute to technical design, story sizing, peer reviews, and continuous improvement.
 Ideal Candidate Profile
 You are a cloud-native, application-side developer who thinks in events, streams, and services—not servers. You design for resiliency, observability, and scale, and you’re comfortable pairing Kafka with AWS serverless to deliver business outcomes.

We sit between autonomy, operations, business development, and customers, turning driverless capability into a real-world product that can be launched, sold, operated, and scaled.
As Waabi rapidly scales from commercial pilots to large-scale driverless deployments, this role serves as the critical integration layer between truck supply, customer commitments, expansion efforts, site activations, and autonomy capabilities. You will manage the execution of the commercial plan, proactively tracking dependencies and mitigating risks to drive clear commercial progress.
We are hiring a Senior Program Manager to own and align the single integrated commercialization plan, ensuring every element converges seamlessly.
While functional program leads manage their respective areas, you will integrate their milestones into the overarching commercial plan. Success relies on sound judgment: identifying critical dependencies, distinguishing real timeline slips, and resolving decision bottlenecks. A year from now, when leadership asks whether we are on track for a launch, a truck delivery or a customer commitment, the answer should be one page, current, and believed by every team on it.
What You'll Do
You will own the integrated commercialization roadmap for trucking and the weekly operating cadence around it. This includes:
Build and own the integrated roadmap that ties customer commitments, OEM truck supply, autonomy and ODD readiness, lane and site activation, Mission Control, operations readiness and Account Management launches to dates, with the dependencies between them made explicit. You own the plan end to end.
Maintain the honest picture: the critical path, the slips, the risks and the decisions needed, surfaced early enough to act on and framed for the people who have to decide.
Lead the execution of key company milestones involving multiple departments at Waabi.
Run the operating cadence, including a weekly cross-functional Truck Program meeting.
Help establish repeatable frameworks, procedures, and decision loops that allow fast and efficient scale.
Produce executive-ready updates and program artifacts.
Communicate clearly with technical, operational, commercial and executive audiences that value first-principles thinking.
What Success Looks Like
Success in this role means the commercial plan converges on purpose rather than by heroics. Specifically, you will have:
Within 90 days, one integrated roadmap that Autonomy, Operations, Sales and Account Management believe, with the Truck Program meeting running off it.
A first driverless launch with no dependency discovered in the final month that was knowable in the first.
Leadership learning about a slip from you, with options, before they learn about it from a customer.
Decisions with a date, an owner and a record, so the same question is not re-decided in three meetings.
Qualifications Required
7+ years in program or product leadership in a complex technical and operational environment (autonomous vehicles, automotive, aerospace, robotics, aviation, defense, logistics or other physical-world deployment).
Track record of integrating programs across teams you did not control, in a business with hardware, software, safety and operations in the loop.
Enough technical fluency to understand why an autonomy or hardware milestone slipped and whether the recovery plan is credible, without needing to be the engineer.
Separates facts, assumptions and risks in how you write and speak; comfortable telling senior people something they do not want to hear, early, with options.
Builds the minimum structure that works and removes or upgrades it when it stops working.
Executive-grade verbal and written communication; most of this role's influence happens in documents and in how a problem is framed.
Set direction for a program others execute, with no direct reports, and being accountable for the outcome anyway.
Strongly Preferred
Ownership mentality: takes initiative and gets into the trenches with key stakeholders.
Varies the degree of detail to the audience and the moment.
Experience running a weekly holistic program review.
Experience taking a physical product from pilot to commercial deployment, where readiness gates and launch dates were real.
Experience working alongside a safety or systems-engineering function on go/no-go decisions.
Experience with OEM or supplier delivery schedules as a dependency in a commercial plan.
Zero-to-one program experience at an early-stage or scaling company.
Nice to have
Direct experience in autonomous trucking, freight or AV commercialization.
Experience working with operations and/or commercial teams.

Waabi US Inc.’s yearly salary ranges are determined based on several factors in accordance with the Company’s compensation practices. Note: The Company provides additional compensation for employees in this role, including equity incentive awards and an annual performance bonus.

Hi, I’m Geo, Ashby’s VP of Product. I joined Ashby August ‘26; read more about why I joined here. https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/all/a-letter-from-chris-geoghegan-on-joining-ashby I’m hiring for multiple Product Managers who will report directly to me. More on the specific product areas below.

At Ashby, we have a unique approach to building products https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles. As a PM, your primary goal is to eliminate frustration and bring delight to our customers. You’ll work with engineers who deeply understand the customer and business problem and own the solution end-to-end. This means that you spend less time writing detailed specs and more time with customers and doing deep product thinking.

Our unique approach is working. We’re growing >100% year over year and have notable customers such as Notion, Linear, OpenAI, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best in class among our peers. We’re backed by amazing investors like Y Combinator, Elad Gil, Lachy Groom, and many more!

PRODUCT AREAS

From day one, we have aimed to build "all-in-one and best-in-class" software for Talent teams. In addition to building a multi-product foundation from day one, we have also focused on enabling customizability and power-user features while keeping Ashby easy to get started with. Doing both is an ambitious undertaking!

We want to continue down this ambitious path in future and add multiple new products, which means we:

 - Are not just building a product, we’re building a platform

 - Need to find a balance between re-usable building blocks and feature-specific behaviour

 - Blend enterprise customizability and ease of use

We also want to continuously delight users. We hear "I never thought one could fall in love with an ATS" quite often, and we want to keep that true for all future products we build.

We are looking for Product Managers who can own the roadmap and strategy for the following areas:

 1. Product Platform: Ashby was designed from the beginning as a multi-product platform. We’re looking for a PM to establish this team and own the shared building blocks, foundational capabilities, and APIs that let product teams move quickly.
    
    - Great fit if you:
      
      - Bring strong technical product judgment and enjoy working on APIs, shared systems, and foundational capabilities
      
      - Know how to balance reusable building blocks with polished, customer-facing product experiences
      
      - Like creating leverage by helping teams ship quickly and consistently while improving what customers directly see and use

 2. AI Platform: You’ll own the Ashby Assistant, Ashby MCP, and the AI platform used across many product surfaces. You’ll help drive shared primitives, such as AI memory and context.
    
    - Great fit if you:
      
      - Have experience building AI-powered products, especially agents, copilots, or workflow automation
      
      - Enjoy shaping shared AI primitives like memory, context, orchestration, and evaluation
      
      - Can translate fast-moving AI capabilities into products that feel useful, reliable, and delightful

During the interview process, we’ll determine which role you're best suited for. We’re also advertising this opening as Senior Product Manager. Both titles describe the same position; please apply once using the title that best reflects your experience.

YOUR ROLE

 - Drive Impact: Deeply understand our customers and ship impactful product improvements and investments to maintain our strong velocity.

 - Quality: Apply your strong product taste and sound judgement to deliver solutions that are both powerful and a joy to use. Use your judgment to identify areas where we need to improve quality before shipping.

 - Prioritization and Strategy: Maintain a roadmap to ensure engineering is never blocked, and set a compelling strategy and vision for the next 6-18 months.

 - Customer Research: Spend time with customers and customer-facing teams. Synthesize customer feedback, research, and competitive intel to drive smart prioritization choices.

 - Execution Excellence: Set the pace for your product area by identifying bottlenecks, scoping effectively, and driving projects toward high-impact releases. Stay close to engineering work to navigate tradeoffs, manage technical risks, and resolve execution challenges.

 - Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner across go-to-market teams to bring the features and products your team builds to the market. Anticipate and plan for the needs to help inform pricing, marketing, and customer support.

 - Ownership and reliability: follow through on commitments, manage time ruthlessly, respond promptly to stakeholders, and communicate proactively when priorities or timelines change.

YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You have an unnatural curiosity and excitement about the end-user and the jobs they do

 - You bring an Engineering mindset to product problems and can think through edge cases and understand how to extend our underlying platform to create leverage

 - You can demonstrate taste - you care about the quality of the products you build and use

 - You're an excellent writer and synthesizer; you bring product knowledge and clarity to the entire organization and enable Engineers with product insights

 - You can build a thesis for prioritization and communicate priorities using a sound strategy that combines principled thinking, research, and data

 - You leverage tools and processes to build operational excellence into your product process

 - You have a strong business sense and understand how product and GTM should collaborate, how your features may be monetized, and how product priorities fit into larger business priorities

YOU MAY NOT BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You prefer to specify exactly what Engineering should build rather than give engineers room to own the solution.

 - You dislike written documentation and prefer to manage the team via meetings and quick Slack messages.

 - You’re primarily interested in shipping features and not thinking through how to make them reusable platform capabilities.

 - You don’t enjoy doing deep research yourself and prefer to outsource that UX research, market research, and data teams.

 - You’re uncomfortable moving with urgency, making tradeoffs, and reprioritizing when new information emerges.

 - You’re primarily motivated by achieving a metric more than delivering a great product experience for customers.

WE WORK DIFFERENTLY

At Ashby, the role of Product Managers is different from what I’ve seen in most product orgs. At a high level, PMs are responsible for shipping impactful product changes at high velocity, consistently and over an extended period. When we think about impactful product changes, our primary goal is to remove frustration and add delight.

At many organizations, PMs are required to write detailed specs that handle every edge case. Designers are required to mock up every pixel. At Ashby, it’s different. We believe individual contributors do their best work when they have a deep understanding of the end user and the business, and ownership of the solution. This is reflected in the engineers Ashby hires: they own projects end-to-end and deeply understand the problems they are solving. PMs are expected to give significant white space in their specs. As a result, PMs can spend less time managing tickets and more time with customers and thinking deeply about the product strategy.

At Ashby, PMs need to be the pace-setters for their product areas. This means they bring a healthy level of impatience and time-paranoia to the table. This does not mean cutting corners or demanding that engineers work unreasonable hours. As a PM, you can help engineers by managing the project scope well, identifying when it’s appropriate to bring in help, or being ruthless about prioritization.

For PM roles at Ashby, we believe great products are built through deep thinking and a clear understanding of user needs. A major part of your role involves conducting thorough user research to uncover underlying customer problems and translating those insights into well-reasoned product strategies.

Finally, Ashby isn’t simply an ATS. Right from the foundations, it was designed to be much more than that. It’s a platform modelled around how organizations (from early-stage startups to massive enterprises) think about recruiting, managing, and retaining top talent. As a PM at Ashby, you should, over time, get familiar with our most common building blocks. You’ll invest not only in product improvements but in platform thinking.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

If this also sounds exciting to you, please apply. We review every application and aim to get back to candidates within 2-3 days. For candidates that advance to the interview process, here is what you can expect:

 1. Intro Call - 30 mins

 2. Product Experience Deep Dive - 1 hour

 3. Product Exercise - 1 hour

 4. Final Round Interview - 2 hours
    Mostly focused on cross-functional Interviews to meet more of the team. This is a critical hire for us and a role that will touch a lot of functions - we want to make sure you'll meet folks you'll be working closely with.

BENEFITS

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year.

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - $250/month tool budget plus access to Claude, Cursor, and Codex with generous token budgets.

 - If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, which is also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

To request reasonable accommodations, please contact hiring@ashbyhq.com.

About Behavox 
 About the Role 
 The Senior FP&A Analyst owns Behavox's core financial model — its architecture, the accounting beneath it, and the forecasts and analysis the company plans and decides by. The role exists to change decisions, not report them: it turns the numbers into the choices leadership actually faces. It reads and integrates budgets into the model, but does not run the budgeting cycle.
 The same analyst builds the valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma models behind every acquisition — evaluating targets, running diligence, and folding closed deals into a single consolidated view. This work is periodic and must be carried alone when it arrives; the steady state is the operating model and SaaS forecasting.
 This is a high-autonomy role that works without a detailed brief and sets the modeling standard others build on. It is accountable for the accuracy and integrity of the numbers, and for turning them into recommendations sharp enough to act on — the downside case included, not just the point estimate — for senior leadership, the board, and investors. It pressure-tests the assumptions behind every result, works fluently with modern tooling and AI, and compounds that edge by learning relentlessly. Its influence comes from the rigor and reach of the analysis, not from authority: it owns the model and the truth it tells, not the decisions made from it.
 What You'll Bring 
 Financial Model & Accounting Foundations — Understands the architecture of integrated three-statement and operating models and the accounting that underpins them, including SaaS revenue recognition and cost treatment. Understands how the company's budgets are built and how to integrate them accurately into the core financial model.
 Forecasting & SaaS Unit Economics — Understands bottom-up short-term forecasting, driver-based long-term modeling, and the SaaS metrics that reveal business performance. Connects movements in those metrics to their underlying drivers and the operating levers that can change them.
 Mergers, Acquisitions & Integration — Understands acquisition valuation, purchase accounting, combined-entity projections, and consolidation mechanics sufficiently to evaluate targets and integrate completed acquisitions into the financial model.
 Business & Commercial Acumen — Understands in depth how the business and its functions generate revenue and incur costs, including the underlying revenue drivers, cost structure, and operating levers. Applies this knowledge to identify inconsistencies and challenge financial results and assumptions.
 Financial Systems & AI Tooling — Understands Google Sheets, Excel, AI, and automation capabilities sufficiently to determine how they should be applied to financial modeling and analysis. Distinguishes where automation can improve speed and control from where financial judgment and manual validation must remain.
 What You'll Do 
 Financial Model Ownership — Builds and maintains the core three-statement and operating model using robust architecture, accounting logic, scenario and sensitivity layers, and integrated budgets, owning the accuracy of every output and the integrity of every assumption to provide reliable forecasts and analysis for company planning and decision-making.
 Acquisition Modeling & Integration — Builds valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma combined-entity models by independently evaluating targets, supporting due diligence, and consolidating closed deals to provide a complete financial view of acquisition implications and the combined business.
 Business-Review Reporting — Drives the financial substance of monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews with the broader FP&A team by translating model outputs and performance drivers into a clear narrative that enables senior management, the board, and investors to understand results and their implications.
 Metrics Analysis & Business Partnering — Diagnoses financial and SaaS metric movements by identifying operating drivers, pressure-testing assumptions, and modeling relevant levers and downside cases to give decision-makers evidence-based recommendations they can act on.
 AI-Enabled Productivity — Applies AI and spreadsheet automation to recurring financial workflows by automating appropriate work and strengthening data validation while retaining judgment over what remains manual to reduce cycle time without compromising financial integrity.
 What We Offer 
 A highly attractive benefits package, including competitive cash compensation, and an equity award aligned with long-term value creation.
 Modern, comfortable offices in Toronto and Montreal. This is a hybrid role (1 day in office). 
 About Our Process 
During the process we will begin by exploring the core factors regarding salary and location along with core experience and skills and values alignment. We will then deep dive explore the critical technical competencies we have identified for the role, and then we will deep dive in behavioral competencies.

Deep Origin is a biotechnology company building an operating system for science that transforms how life science research is conducted. Our AI-powered platforms simulate biology, streamline R&D workflows, and enable scientists to model complex biological systems at scale. 
 Deep Origin leads the PREDICTS consortium, funded by ARPA-H under the CATALYST program, to build in silico models that predict human drug safety and toxicity. As part of this work we are scaling our capabilities in whole-human modeling and predictive toxicology. 
About the role
 Deep Origin is building VHAT, the Virtual Human Avatars of Toxicology. VHAT takes a molecule, a dose and a patient population and predicts organ-level human toxicity before a compound is synthesized or dosed. Metabolism sits at the heart of that chain. What a drug becomes, which enzymes act on it and how fast they act determine what each organ is exposed to, and every predicted metabolite is screened for its own off-target and organ liabilities. The Metabolism group builds four connected models: drug-metabolizing enzyme, site of metabolism, metabolite structure, and enzyme kinetics. As the group’s leader, you will own those models, mentor the team that builds them, and drive integration of their predicted parameters into the physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model that governs exposure across the VHAT.
 Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time. 
 A PhD in computational chemistry, cheminformatics, drug metabolism, computational biology, pharmacology or a related field.
 Deep, hands-on expertise in drug metabolism . You understand CYP and non-CYP enzymes, sites and products of metabolism, enzyme kinetics and clearance, and you can judge whether a prediction is chemically and biologically sound.
 A strong track record in computational modeling , either as a model builder or as an expert end-user. This includes machine learning for molecular property or reactivity prediction, and mechanistic or kinetic modeling, including ODE-based models, parameter estimation, and Bayesian or frequentist inference. You work fluently in Python.
 Demonstrated rigor in model validation. You have designed appropriate data splits, defined applicability domains, and run external or blinded benchmarks, and you can explain the limits of a model as clearly as its strengths.
 Experience leading a scientific team and delivering against milestones and deadlines.
 Clear written and spoken communication with scientists, partners and funders. 
Strongly preferred 
 This role owns the link between metabolism and whole-body exposure, so PBPK experience will weigh heavily in our decision.
 Hands-on experience building or parameterizing PBPK models in Simcyp, GastroPlus, PK-Sim, SimBiology or a custom ODE framework.
 Experience translating in vitro or predicted intrinsic clearance into in vivo hepatic clearance and human PK, including the use of IVIVE scaling factors and an understanding of where they tend to fail.
 Experience using PBPK to assess metabolic drug-drug interactions, such as CYP inhibition and induction.
 Experience combining machine learning predictions with mechanistic PK models, and carrying their uncertainty into downstream predictions.
 Nice to have 
 Experience with metabolomics or LC-MS metabolite identification data.
 Experience running data curation at scale, including annotation standards and quality control.
 Experience on government-funded research programs with milestone-based reporting.
 Exposure to regulatory science, such as FDA guidance on new approach methodologies, model-informed drug development or the ISTAND program.
 Familiarity with medicinal chemistry and how metabolism liabilities are addressed during lead optimization.
 Responsibilities
 Lead a team of computational scientists and data curators across sites. Set scientific direction, priorities and review standards for each model, and develop the people who build them.
 Own the roadmap and release gates for the four metabolism models. Decide when a model is ready for the VHAT platform, for use as a standalone product, and for external review.
 Own the metabolism-to-PBPK integration. Define which parameters pass to the PBPK model, how predicted or in vitro clearance is scaled to in vivo hepatic clearance, and how the combined model is checked against clinical PK and drug-drug interaction data. Work with PBPK modelers so that parent and metabolite exposure flow correctly into the organ models.
 Design validation experiments that hold up to outside scrutiny. This includes leakage-aware data splits, applicability-domain and confidence reporting, predictions locked before new experimental data arrive, and external, blinded and independent benchmarks.
 Set the data strategy for a field where high-quality labels are scarce. Plan curation targets and throughput, oversee AI-assisted literature mining with expert quality control, support data licensing, and design wet-lab experiments with partners (recombinant enzymes, human liver microsomes, hepatocytes), including active-learning compound selection.
 Extend coverage beyond CYP Phase I metabolism to Phase II enzymes (UGT, SULT), FMO, AOX and multistep metabolic networks, and scope how enzyme polymorphism and population variability enter the models.
 Manage external relationships with consortium partners, contract research organizations, academic reviewers and independent validation teams.
 Author technical milestone reports and present results to ARPA-H. Contribute metabolism content to grant proposals and to regulatory engagement on new approach methodologies.
 Work with the modeling and integration teams to carry uncertainty from the metabolism models through PBPK to the final organ-level risk.
 What success looks like 
 In the first 6 months, you will have taken ownership of the four models and the team. Metabolite identity and enzyme-isoform predictions will be released on the VHAT platform and reported to ARPA-H. Predicted clearance and kinetic parameters will be passed into the PBPK model with documented methods and scaling assumptions. Prospective predictions on new wet-lab metabolism data will have been locked in advance and scored. A first version of the kinetics model will be in place, and you will have set a clear plan for curation throughput, enzyme coverage and population variability.
 By 12 months, the metabolism models will have been tested by an independent validation team on held-out data. Metabolite concentration profiles will feed PBPK for both parent drugs and metabolites, and from there the organ models. Coverage will extend beyond CYP Phase I enzymes, and confidence estimates from the metabolism models will carry through to VHAT risk outputs. The team will be running on a roadmap you set, with each model's strengths and limits clearly documented.
 Why join us 
 This is a chance to lead metabolism science inside a program that links atomic-level predictions to whole-human safety outcomes. The work is hard because the data are scarce, and it matters because toxicity remains a leading cause of clinical failure. 
 Competitive compensation package with meaningful equity.
 Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage.
 A remote-friendly culture across the U.S. and Europe, with flexible, cross-time-zone working. 
 Opportunity to shape the future of health, longevity, and our ability to simulate life.
 Annual team gatherings and company events.

PERPLEXITY API PLATFORM

Perplexity innovates at the frontier of AI infrastructure, search, and orchestration to serve the world's most discerning users. The Perplexity API Platform brings our technology to the world's most discerning developers. From exabyte-scale knowledge indexes to codegen-first agent runtimes, the building blocks behind Perplexity's applications are some of the most battle-tested AI systems in the industry.

We believe these same building blocks can and should power the aspirations of builders everywhere. It's one thing to solve planet-scale retrieval, long-horizon orchestration, and other foundational AI challenges within a single product ecosystem. The true measure of success is to turn those solutions into elegant APIs that delight developers and agents alike. Our API Platform delivers frontier intelligence to thousands of customers: startups, trillion-dollar enterprises, U.S. and allied governments, and everyone in between.

We've achieved incredible scale, yet we're just getting started. Join us to build tools for curious minds.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

Perplexity is seeking strong engineers with a passion for delivering frontier intelligence and infrastructure to developers. Our company builds technology that reshapes how people search, reason, and interact with the world around them. Week after week, we observe increasing demand for programmatic interfaces to that technology. The API Platform engineering team is charged with designing, implementing, and scaling these interfaces.

As a member of our team, you'll work on an eclectic portfolio spanning distributed systems, performance optimization, agent orchestration, and frontier topics that often change with each passing month. Throughout this work, you'll prioritize great developer and agent experience alike. You'll also define technical strategy for how we scale to meet compounding growth exponentials (number of customers, agents per customer, compute/retrieval per agent, etc.).




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, build, and operate mission-critical APIs that provide our customers the building blocks for frontier intelligence.

 - Own and evolve the API gateway and routing layer: authentication, authorization, rate limiting and quotas, usage metering, and request routing across heterogeneous upstream services.

 - Build the paved road for API services: standardized service scaffolding, container builds, CI/CD, Kubernetes and Helm deployment, and progressive rollouts with fast rollback, so a new API product goes from idea to production in days, not weeks.

 - Build API governance into the platform: contract-first schemas, breaking-change detection in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from a single source of truth.

 - Unify cross-cutting capabilities (billing and usage, rate limiting, organization and identity settings, analytics and observability) so every API product gets them by default instead of rebuilding them.

 - Ensure low latency and high throughput through aggressive performance optimization (including on upstream systems).

 - Harden system security and reliability across heterogeneous compute environments, and operate what you build: SLOs, on-call, and incident response.

 - Collaborate across teams to bring novel frontier capabilities into the API Platform, and partner with infrastructure teams on compute, networking, secrets, and security.

 - Continually reimagine the customer needs of tomorrow (and the architectures to serve those needs), while faithfully serving the customer workloads of today.

 - Uphold engineering excellence through design reviews, code quality, and internal documentation.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 5+ years of backend engineering experience with Python, Go, or Rust, including significant time building platforms or infrastructure used by other engineering teams.

 - Strong understanding of high-traffic API design: schema evolution & versioning, idempotency, authentication patterns, rate limiting, and performance tuning.

 - Hands-on experience building and operating API gateways, reverse proxies, or routing layers: authentication and authorization, rate limiting and quotas, request routing, traffic shaping, and per-request observability.

 - Experience building API governance tooling: contract-first API design, breaking-change detection and API linting in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from the contract.

 - Platform depth across the build and deploy path: you have owned CI/CD pipelines, container builds and base images, infrastructure as code, and progressive delivery (canary or blue-green) on a major cloud.

 - A track record of owning a platform end to end: identifying the need, designing it, aligning the teams that depend on it, shipping it, and operating it, while raising the engineering bar for the teams building on it.

 - Strong customer empathy and product sense, ensuring the APIs you build are ergonomic, well-documented, and easy to adopt for developers and agents alike.

Strong plus:

 - Experience with modern AI APIs (including latency tuning, streaming, model orchestration, emerging technical standards).

 - Usage-based billing and metering systems, multi-tenant organization and identity models, and usage analytics pipelines.

 - Observability for API platforms: structured logging pipelines, metrics, tracing, and SLO tooling.

About Clutch: 
 Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, delivering a seamless, hassle-free car buying and selling experience to drivers everywhere. Customers can browse hundreds of cars from the comfort of their home, get the right one delivered to their door, and enjoy peace of mind with our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee… and that’s just the beginning.
 Named one of Canada's top growing Companies two years in a row and also awarded a spot on LinkedIn's Top Canadian Startups list, we're looking to add curious, hard-working, and driven individuals to our growing team.
 Headquartered in Toronto, Clutch was founded in 2017. Clutch is backed by a number of world-class investors, including Canaan, BrandProject, Real Ventures, D1 Capital, and Upper90. To learn more, visit clutch.ca
 About the role: 
 For most of our customers, buying a car is also one of the biggest financial decisions they'll make. That's why we built Clutch's financial services offering, and we're hiring a Senior Data Scientist to help shape what it becomes.
 Your mission is to bring a financing-first lens to the entire buyer journey. That means helping customers understand what they can afford earlier, feel confident in their choices, and move from browsing to buying with fewer surprises.
 This role starts analysis-heavy. Your first priority will be building a deep understanding of how customers engage with financing today: where they start, where they get stuck, and what helps them move forward. From there, you'll build the models, tools, and experiments that shape how customers experience financing at Clutch, from pre-qualification through purchase.
 This is a rare chance to join early and help define how one of Canada's fastest-growing auto retailers approaches financing. You'll sit on Clutch's data team and work closely with our financial services, product, marketing, and engineering teams, and your work will be visible, measurable, and directly tied to both the customer experience and the business.
 What you'll do: 
 Help define what Cleo becomes. As one of the first data scientists on our financial services work, your analysis will shape the roadmap and play a key role in its delivery.
 Go deep on buyer journey and financing funnel data to understand how customers explore, compare, and choose financing, and where the experience can improve.
 Build the models that power a financing-first shopping experience, surfacing cars customers can realistically afford and helping them understand their monthly payment before they fall in love with a car.
 Predict financing intent and readiness from on-site behaviour so we can meet customers with the right information at the right moment.
 Own pre-qualification end-to-end, from how many customers start it, to where they drop off, to how it changes what they buy, and use those insights to give customers clarity earlier in their journey.
 Model how down payment, trade-in value, and term choices shape customer decisions, and build tools that help customers explore those trade-offs themselves.
 Design and analyze experiments to test new ways of presenting financing across the site and purchase flow.
 Quantify how financing drives Clutch's business, including conversion, order value, and customer lifetime value, and turn your findings into clear recommendations on where to invest next.
 Partner with Clutch data engineering and our external partners to define the data foundations our financial services work needs to scale.
 Work with Clutch’s external financial services partners to refine journeys and programs in ways that improve the experience, conversion and risk performance.
 What we're looking for: 
 Must Haves 
 5+ years of experience as a Data Scientist or in a highly analytical role, with a track record of work that drove real business decisions.
 Decision modeling experience: You've built models or frameworks that shaped real outcomes, such as how customers are guided, what they're shown, or how a funnel is optimized.
 Analysis first: Strong SQL and Python, and you're comfortable starting with messy data and ambiguous questions and working your way to a clear answer.
 Statistical rigor: Solid statistical fundamentals, experimentation experience, and a disciplined approach to validation.
 Customer mindset: You care about how your work shows up for the end customer, not just the metric it moves.
 Excellent communication: You can explain complex trade-offs clearly to business leaders and hold a strong point of view.
 Nice to Have 
 Experience in fintech, consumer finance, or auto finance.
 Experience with e-commerce funnels, personalization, or customer journey analytics.
 Experience deploying models into production.
 Experience helping build a new product or business line from an early stage.

Sadie is building technology for hospitality.
 We're looking for an account executive to win new restaurant customers around major cities in Canada, and to run every deal yourself from the first lead to the signed agreement.
 This is a field role. You'll find restaurants through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits, then meet owners in person and show them Sadie working on their own calls. You'll work with onboarding and customer success, so that what you sell goes live well. You'll carry monthly and quarterly targets and own the forecast behind them.
 You decide where to spend your time and which deals to pursue, within agreed pricing and terms. AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research restaurants before a visit, prepare demos, draft proposals and follow-ups, and plan your territory. You're responsible for the quality of everything that goes out under your name.
 What we value
 Sound judgement about which deals are real.
 Taking responsibility for your number and finishing work without being chased.
 Understanding how a restaurant makes money, and caring whether Sadie improves it.
 Curiosity about why a deal was lost, and a willingness to change your approach.
 The honesty to say a deal is slipping before the forecast says it for you.
 What you'll do
 Win new restaurants, from first visit to signed agreement 
 Most of your time goes on live deals, and most of those deals happen in person. You'll sit down with owners and general managers in their restaurants to learn how the phone is handled today: who answers it, what gets missed during service, and what those missed calls cost in bookings and orders. Then you'll demo Sadie against that picture.
 You'll scope what the restaurant needs, write the proposal, negotiate terms and get the agreement signed. 
 Most of the judgement is in qualification. A good demo with someone who can't sign, or a restaurant Sadie can't serve yet, costs you weeks. You're expected to spot that early and move on.
 Build your own pipeline across your territory 
 You'll generate your own leads through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits. That means planning which neighbourhoods and restaurant groups to work, walking in at the right time of day, and following up until you get a meeting.
 Hit your targets with a forecast you can defend 
 You're measured against monthly and quarterly sales targets, and the expectation is that you hit them consistently. You'll keep every opportunity accurate in HubSpot, so that stage, value and close date mean something to the people who plan around them.
 Represent Sadie where restaurant people meet 
 You'll attend local industry events, restaurant meetups and trade shows across your geography. You'll decide which ones are worth the evening, run the conversations there, and turn them into meetings within the week.
 For a lot of operators, you'll be the first person from Sadie they meet. What they hear from you is what they'll repeat to other owners.
 Hand over accounts that go live well 
 The restaurant buys Sadie, but the guest ringing to book a table decides whether it works. You'll give onboarding and customer success a written record of what you promised, what the owner expects, and what could go wrong.
 If you oversell, the owner finds out on a Friday night and the guest pays for it. Set expectations you can stand behind.
 What you'll bring
 At least 2 years in a closing sales role, selling software or services to businesses.
 A record of meeting targets, and the ability to explain how you did it.
 Experience running the whole cycle yourself, from prospecting through to signature.
 Comfort with in-person selling, including cold visits and demos in front of a busy owner.
 Strong discovery skills. You can find out what an operator needs in fifteen minutes between services.
 Clear written communication. Your proposals and follow-ups are accurate and short.
 An honest forecast. You'd rather call a deal lost than carry it for another month.
 You use AI every day for research, preparation and drafting, and you check what it produces.
 You organise your own week across a territory and follow through without being managed.
 Useful experience
 Selling to restaurants or other hospitality operators.
 Working in a restaurant yourself, front of house or in management.
 Selling reservations, POS, telephony or other restaurant technology.
 An existing network among restaurant owners in your territory.
 Selling AI products to non-technical buyers.
 Being an early sales hire at a startup.
 Who will enjoy this role
 You like finding out how a business really works. When an owner says they miss calls at seven on a Saturday, you want to know how many, what those calls were for, and what happened to the guest who hung up.
 In a single week you might walk into six restaurants before lunch service, run a demo at a bar between shifts, spend an evening at a trade show, and sit with onboarding to sort out an account you signed. Your schedule follows the restaurant day, and some of your best conversations will happen at three in the afternoon or late at night.
 The hard parts are specific. Owners are busy and sceptical, and many will turn you away mid-service. You'll hear no far more often than yes, and you'll still need to be back through the next door the same afternoon. Some of the material you'd expect to have, such as local case studies or a settled playbook, may not exist yet, and you'll help build it while carrying a number.
 Why this role matters
 Sadie is building technology for hospitality. Restaurants lose revenue to calls nobody picks up, and our product exists to answer them.
 This role is how Sadie reaches the restaurants in your geography. You decide who to visit and how each customer starts. The agreements you sign affect revenue, what onboarding and customer success inherit, and what a guest hears when they ring to book a table.
 You'll own new restaurant business across your territory, with the authority to decide how Sadie wins it.

Who We Are

North Vector Dynamics is a Canadian-owned and controlled defence technology company specializing in precision interception, autonomy, and advanced propulsion. NVD is building a full-spectrum missile capability, from counter-UAS solutions to hypersonics, designed to serve and defend NATO member states and their allies and partners.

About the Role

North Vector Dynamics is building next-generation defence systems, and the CM70 is moving from prototype builds to a controlled, repeatable production line. We’re looking for a QA Compliance Lead/Process Engineer to own how our platforms are built on the shop floor: assembly routings, work instructions, quality data collection, and the continuous improvement of all three across supply chains.

Reporting to the Head of Manufacturing directly, you’ll be the lead process owner for our pilot line and the first engineer to deploy our Manufacturing Execution System (MES) on it, turning hard-won prototype know-how into a documented, traceable, audit-ready process.

In addition, you will stand up our initial control plans, and quality assurance system(s) documentation to prepare the team for AS9100 certification; and assist the Manufacturing Engineering team in standing up a proper supply chain system.

This is a ground-floor role for someone who is technically rigorous, data-driven, and energized by building systems from a clean sheet rather than inheriting them. You’ll work side by side with our technicians and design engineers, along with senior leadership and your work will define how North Vector Dynamics builds hardware as we scale.

If you want to stand up a production system that will one day support platforms in the field, saves lives, and serves sovereign national interest - this role was written for you.

What You’ll Do

Process Engineering

• Map current CM70 assembly and build the production routings, process flows, and station layouts for our pilot line: defining each operation, its inputs, tooling, and quality checks.

• Write and maintain electronic work instructions, SOPs, and visual job aids under document and revision control, so every technician builds the same way, every time.

• Lead the process side of our MES rollout: configuring routings, station consumption, conducting time studies for takt optimizations, serialization and genealogy, and data collection points so every build is traceable from component to completed workpiece.

• Define critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics, inspection points, and quality gates for each operation; lead PFMEAs and control plans, and feed design-for-manufacturability (DFM) input back to engineering and drive overall improvements to the PD cycle.

• Stand up our non-conformance (NCR/MRB) workflow and drive root cause and corrective action, closing the loop between what fails on the floor and what changes in the process or design.

• Build processes that meet AS9100 and Controlled Goods Program requirements: supporting first article inspections, process validation, and internal dry-run audits using MES traceability records.

• Track yield, cycle time, first-pass yield, and OEE; use data and SPC to find and remove waste and variation, and lead kaizen, 5S, and line-balancing efforts as volumes increase.

• Support the layout, fixture, tooling, and equipment specification for our new manufacturing space, and help define how MES, ERP, and PLM/PDM data flow together.

• Assess engineering changes for their impact on routings, tooling, and work instructions before release, and train technicians on every new or updated process.

Quality & Compliance

• Build and own our Quality Management System from the ground up: (supplier) internal quality manual, procedures, document and record control, and the gap assessment and roadmap that take us to AS9100 certification, serving as the primary contact with our registrar.

• Establish and run our internal audit program, and host customer, registrar, and government audits (including Controlled Goods Program inspections), driving every finding through to verified closure.

• Own the corrective and preventive action (CAPA) system and the Material Review Board (MRB): dispositioning non-conforming product, and reporting quality performance to senior leadership through regular management reviews.

• Stand up supplier quality alongside the Manufacturing Engineering team: approved supplier list, supplier qualification and audits, incoming and source inspection, flow-down of quality and regulatory requirements on purchase orders, and supplier corrective action requests.

• Own product acceptance and configuration conformity: ensuring every as-built matches its released configuration, approving final release and certificates of conformance, and maintaining build records to contract retention requirements.

• Put in place the core programs a defence supplier is held to; calibration and measurement system analysis, counterfeit parts prevention, foreign object debris (FOD) control, and ESD control.

• Keep the business compliant with Controlled Goods Program, export control, and contract quality requirements, and train the team so quality and compliance are built into daily work rather than inspected in afterward.

• Step into whatever the mission demands: this is a startup, no two weeks will look the same!

What You Bring

Required

• A bachelor’s degree (minimum) in manufacturing, mechanical, industrial, mechatronics, or aerospace engineering, or an equivalent technical discipline from an accredited program and institution.

• 3+ years as a process, manufacturing, or industrial engineer in a hardware production environment, with a track record of processes you built or materially improved.

• Hands-on experience writing work instructions, routings, and SOPs, and managing them under document and revision control.

• Working knowledge of PFMEA, control plans, and structured root cause analysis (8D, 5 Whys, fishbone), and the discipline to see corrective actions through to closure.

• Practical lean manufacturing experience: value stream mapping, standard work, 5S, and kaizen applied on a real shop floor, not just in a classroom.

• Comfort with data: building, analyzing, and presenting yield, cycle-time, and quality metrics in Excel, Power BI, or similar tools to make an ambiguous problem clear.

• Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings (including GD&T), bills of materials, and wiring diagrams, and to work within a CAD/PDM environment.

• Hands-on experience building or maintaining a quality management system to AS9100 or ISO 9001, including document control, CAPA, MRB, and internal audits.

• Experience leading or hosting third-party, customer, or regulatory audits, and owning the response to findings.

• Supplier quality experience: qualifying and auditing suppliers, managing incoming inspection, and driving supplier corrective actions.

• The confidence to hold the line on quality and compliance with peers and senior leadership, paired with the judgment to find practical solutions in a fast-moving startup.

• Eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance and registration under the Controlled Goods Program; active clearance is a significant asset.

• A builder’s mindset: you take ownership of the system, not just the task, and you’re as comfortable on the floor with a technician as you are in a design review.

Preferred

• P.Eng. or EIT designation, or eligibility for registration in Alberta or conversion from eligible province(s).

• Prior experience in a UAS, aerospace, high volume, or defence manufacturing environment operating under AS9100 or a similar quality management system.

• Experience taking an organization through initial AS9100 certification. ISO9001 is considered a direct comparable preferred skillset/experience.

• AS9100 lead auditor certification, or ASQ certification such as CQE, CQA, or CMQ/OE.

• Familiarity with the Controlled Goods Program, export controls (EIPA, ITAR), counterfeit parts prevention (AS5553/AS6174), FOD prevention (AS9146), and defence contract quality requirements such as AQAP 2110.

• Direct experience deploying or configuring an MES, including electronic work instructions and serialized genealogy.

• Exposure to ERP and PLM/PDM systems (Autodesk Vault, SolidWorks PDM/PLM, Arena, or similar) and how they integrate with shop-floor execution.

• Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or higher, with demonstrated SPC knowledge.

• An electromechanical assembly background: wiring harnesses, PCB handling and ESD control, torque control, adhesives, or composites.

• Experience launching a new production line or ramping volume, ideally in a startup or scale-up, including fixture and tooling design.

Why North Vector Dynamics

• Real ownership from day one: the systems and processes you help build will be foundational to how this company operates for years to come.

• A tight-knit, high-calibre team that moves fast, holds each other to a high standard, and doesn’t waste time on bureaucracy for its own sake.

Cerebras is building a new generation of disaggregated AI inference systems that combine GPU-accelerated prefill with ultra-fast decode on the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine.

We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to build and evolve the ML API layer that makes this heterogeneous serving system accessible, reliable, and easy to use. You will own significant features and components across our inference APIs, model integration layer, and request-routing services, delivering a consistent experience across models and accelerator backends.

This role sits at the intersection of machine learning systems, API design, model serving, and distributed systems. You will translate evolving model capabilities and customer requirements into clear designs, lead implementation across multiple components, and carry features through validation, rollout, and production operation. Your work will help ensure that streaming, sampling, tool use, structured outputs, multimodal inputs, and model configuration behave correctly and consistently.

You will work closely with model enablement, compiler, runtime, cloud infrastructure, product, and customer-facing teams, as well as customers directly. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role with opportunities to lead small project teams, mentor engineers, and improve the quality and reliability of production inference software.

Responsibilities

 - Own features end to end. Design, implement, test, and operate features for chat completions, text generation, streaming, model configuration, tool calling, structured outputs, multimodal inputs, and emerging inference capabilities.

 - Lead multi-component delivery. Write clear design documents, evaluate technical tradeoffs, break projects into deliverable milestones, and coordinate implementation with a small group of engineers and partner teams.

 You'll grow the top of the funnel by reaching new viewers who fit our audience.  You'll be responsible for what we make, why we make it, how we package and produce it, and whether it worked. You'll work directly with Richard and the leadership team to set direction, goals and KPI's and lead, hire and manage a creative team underneath.

 Strategy and ideation: own the channel's growth goals, metrics and KPIs.  Analytics: review what worked, what didn't and what to change next.  Team: hire, onboard and manage editors, designers and writers. Coach people to improve and write procedures and checklists that help the team make good decisions independently.

 You have a deep passion for YouTube (storytelling and psychology), and an understanding of channel growth.
